problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ x \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Given that the scalar projection of $a$ onto $b$ is $0,$ find the value of $x.$
worked_solution:
Since $a$ is a nonzero vector, its scalar projection onto another nonzero vector $b$ equals zero only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
a⊥b\,⟹\,a\cdot b=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & ={a}_{x}\cdot {b}_{x}+{a}_{y}\cdot {b}_{y}+{a}_{z}\cdot {b}_{z} \\  & =0\cdot (-2)+(-2)\cdot x+1\cdot 2 \\  & =2-2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =0 \\ 2-2x & =0 \\ 2x & =2 \\ x & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
